title: The name Ardenna
text:
Hey Claude, how do you pronounce Ardenna?  

"Ardenna" is pronounced ar-DEN-uh (with the stress on the middle syllable).
It's the genus name for shearwaters - those incredible long-distance seabirds that spend most of their lives at sea, gliding low over the waves. A fitting name for a bluewater cruising yacht!
author: Doug

title: Looking for a 1,500nm logbook entry?
text:
We are heading south this Autumn to the Dominican Republic and would like some crew to join the fun.  This is not a potential or a maybe but a confirmed passage to leave Ardenna in Puerto Bahía Marina in Samaná, DR this November 2026.  

Over Halloween weekend, we will be meeting up with other members of the Bluewater Sailing Club in Newport, RI to prep, plan, and commune before heading out to sea together.  Specifically, we will be at a dock at the Newport Yachting Center October 30 - November 1 leaving (weather permitting of course) for what should be a 9 -12 day passage directly to the DR.

Are you interested in joining us?  This should be a fun, offshore passage, with a wide range of weather, currents, and marine life.  Starting in cold New England, we will layer our wool under bibs and hoodies while enjoying the warmth of the full boat Webasto hydronic heater off watch.  Feeling like a cup of tea?  Turn on the electric kettle whenever you want.

Leaving Newport, we head East and cut the Gulf Stream to then start a straight shot South taking Bermuda to port.  Within a few days the weather will warm and we’ll ditch the wool, and need to start washing the salt off our sunnies.  A few more days after that you’ll need sun screen for your legs as shorts become the order of the day until we get South of Florida and then it will just be hot (can someone please open another hatch?!)

The weather windows open and close quickly in New England in Autumn so some flexibility in Samana arrival will be needed; however, the total trip should be somewhere between 8 - 12 days.  We greatly prefer to sail but do not mind motoring to keep things moving along, charge off batteries and make some hot water.  Everyone should have their own bunks and locker, and a fresh water shower every few days.  We pay for food, customs, visas, and transportation to Santo Domingo airport.  You pick up the trip to Newport (we can get you in Boston Logan) and the trip home from the DR.

Passage start: Newport Yachting Center, Newport, RI, USA November 1, 2026 (est.)
Passage end: Puerto Bahía Marina, Samaná, Dominican Republic November 14, 2026 (est.)
author: Doug
